acceptanceCriteria: Lane charters supply BASE, outcome, verify file and citation plan up front, and run the post-commit dogfood change/check/seal once, after the last edit, through the finish-lane recipe.
A missing input is refused before any expensive work starts, naming every missing input at once.
Measured over the next batch: dogfood-change invocations per lane median at most 2, with the counts retained.
body: Evidence: owner-requested audit on 2026-10-17 of orchestrator session 03e2afac (Handoff 2026-10-14): 206 Claude Code lane subagents, 374 lane-hours over 77 h wall. Measured from subagent transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/-Users-russelllewis-projects-corvint/03e2afac-.../subagents (tool_use to tool_result timestamps) and live host reads. Toolchain: corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.615, Go 1.27.2, macOS 12-core/64 GB host. Over 206 lanes: dogfood-change ran 855 times (27.9 h, avg 2.0 min), dogfood-check 226 (7.9 h), dogfood-seal 179 (4.5 h). Per-lane dogfood-change count: median 4, tail 17-19. Refusals seen in outputs: `dogfood-change: FAIL not-complete` (58), missing DOGFOOD_OUTCOME/DOGFOOD_VERIFY_FILE (13), `BASE is required` (19). Lanes made 116 edits after their first commit, each forcing a re-bind. 60% of lane time (207 h of 345 h) came after the first commit, 67.5 h of it dogfood. The single finish-lane recipe (V1-1348) exists but lanes are not held to running it once at the terminal boundary. Related: V1-1616 (finish-lane over 600 s).
title: Lanes rerun dogfood-change 4-19 times each; 855 runs cost 28 h where the protocol needs about 2 per lane
